answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by treating trust like water in a lagoon: each established agent holds a finite pool of trust that flows outward through vouches but thins with every hop, so a vertex two steps away carries far less weight than a direct one. Splitting one pool across a hundred newcomers leaves each with a whisper, below the threshold for standing, so every extra fake needs a fresh unit of undiluted trust from a distinct well-connected source - velvet-smooth on the surface, but no farm can stretch one source into a thousand identities.
